reflection_text.10:
The Ontario regime in force Jan 2020 is OSA s.53/73/74 and NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501.

* Bank debt – Canadian Schedule I/II
A – Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank and the security is bonds/non-convertible debt. OSA s.74, NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.7 is an issuer and security based statutory exemption for non-convertible debt of a bank/trust/loan/insurance company carrying on business in Canada. It is not conditioned on accreditation, eligible investor status, minimum amount or size/retail nature of the offering. A is now unanimously treated as prospectus-exempt, textbook Canadian bank-debt case.

* Foreign bank debt
B – JPMorgan Chase is a U.S. chartered bank, not a Bank Act Canada Schedule I/II/III bank. Majority view: the Ontario bank-debt exemption is a Canadian Bank Act exemption; no accredited investor / $150k minimum amount / OM / family-friends basis is pleaded for a large retail Canadian offering, so B is non-compliant. The minority round-0 view that bank status alone suffices is now marginal.

* Private issuer to non-connected person
C – Salary $35k, net assets $10k. Jan 2020 accredited investor thresholds: net assets ≥ $1M excl principal residence or net income ≥ $200k individual / $300k with spouse in each of two most recent years and reasonably expected. No $150k minimum amount, OM or relationship pleaded. Consensus non-compliant.

* Bank equity vs bank debt
D – Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank but distribution is shares. Majority 10/11/2/3/4/6/8/9: bank/financial institution exemption is a non-convertible debt securities exemption; NI 45-106 s.2.9 OM is expressly unavailable to a bank/trust/loan/insurance company. Retail share distribution including zero net asset unemployed purchaser is not covered and no accredited/minimum-amount basis is made out, so D is non-compliant. Minority issuer-based-any-security view has largely retreated.

* Credit union / caisse populaire
E – Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a cooperative credit association federally incorporated under Cooperative Credit Associations Act.
Split persists in round 3:
Broad issuer-based reading – Colleagues 1,5,7,11,12: OSA s.74 and NI 45-106/Rule 45-501 cooperative/credit-union exemption is issuer-based, securities-of-the-issuer, purchaser neutral, not conditioned on accreditation, minimum amount, membership status or provincial nexus. Same policy logic as bank-debt exemption; personal financial circumstances, retail breadth and extra-provincial incorporation irrelevant. Under this reading E is compliant and some argue it is the cleanest compliant example alongside A, even broader than bank exemption as it is not limited to debt.
Strict members-only / provincial nexus reading – Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,9,10: exemption in practice is for membership/share capital issued to members in accordance with enabling legislation and applied to Ontario credit unions; OM unavailable to credit union. Facts plead general retail raise aimed at large number of retail investors in Ontario with no representation take-up limited to members, extra-provincial issuer, non-accredited zero net asset unemployed offeree. Member nexus/provincial nexus not made out, so E is non-compliant as pleaded.

Unresolved / split points: scope of credit-union/co-operative exemption – issuer-based blanket vs members-only/provincial nexus. Bank exemption debt-only vs any security is largely settled debt-only. Foreign bank status settled as Canadian Bank Act required by majority.

Current best synthesis: A is unambiguously compliant; B, C, D are non-compliant on prevailing readings; E is the main disagreement, majority strict reading finding it non-compliant as pleaded, minority issuer-based reading finding it compliant. On conventional straight exam reading only A is unambiguously prospectus-exempt on the facts stated.
reflection_text.4:
The bank-debt / financial-institution exemption remains the anchor.

* A – Bank of China (Canada) bonds to retail. Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank, securities are bonds/non-convertible debt. OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.7 is issuer and security based and is not conditioned on accreditation, eligible investor status, minimum amount or size/retail nature. Consensus in round 3: unambiguously prospectus exempt in Ontario Jan 2020. Teaching nuance raised by Colleague 12: Schedule II / foreign-owned Canadian branch point is routinely used to test the exemption; that doubt is why some put A as less clean than E, but the majority still treats A as the textbook compliant example.

* B – JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large number of Canadian investors. Majority view holds the Ontario bank/financial-institution exemption is a Canadian Bank Act exemption for debt of a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act Canada carrying on business in Canada. JPMorgan Chase is a U.S. chartered bank, not a Bank Act Canada bank. No accredited investor s.2.3, $150k minimum amount s.2.5, family/friends s.2.7 or qualifying OM s.2.9 is pleaded. Non-compliant. Minority Colleague 1/12 in round 0 argued foreign domicile is irrelevant; the majority statutory wording now dominates in round 3.

* C – Private issuer shares to non-connected individual, salary $35k, net assets $10k. Accredited investor thresholds Jan 2020: net assets ≥ $1M ex principal residence or net income ≥ $200k individual / $300k with spouse in each of two most recent years and reasonably expected current year. No $150k minimum amount, no OM, no family/friends/business associates/employee relationship pleaded. Consensus non-compliant.

* D – Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to retail including zero net asset unemployed purchaser. Fairstone is a Bank Act bank, but the statutory bank exemption in Ontario is a non-convertible debt securities exemption. NI 45-106 s.2.9 OM is expressly unavailable to a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company. Bank equity is not covered by the bank-debt exemption on the conventional debt-only reading. No accredited/minimum amount basis made out. Consensus non-compliant. Minority Colleague 5/7 in earlier rounds argued bank exemption is issuer based and covers any security irrespective of form/purchaser net worth; that minority is not prevailing in round 3.

* E – Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to large retail pool, one offeree zero net assets unemployed. Split persists and intensified in round 3.
Issuer-based reading, Colleagues 1,5,7,11,12: Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a cooperative credit association/caisse populaire federally incorporated under the Cooperative Credit Associations Act. OSA s.74 and NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 co-operative credit union exemption is issuer based for securities of a cooperative credit union; it is not conditioned on purchaser accreditation, eligible investor status, minimum amount, membership at time of offer, or Ontario incorporation for a trade occurring in Ontario. The zero net asset/unemployed facts test purchaser neutrality just as retail nature tests the bank-debt exemption for A. On this consistent reading E is prospectus exempt, and some argue it is actually cleaner than A because the credit-union exemption covers equity.
Strict members-only/Ontario nexus reading, Colleagues 10,2,3,4,6,8,9: exemption is in practice a members’ securities exemption applied to membership/share capital issued to members in accordance with enabling legislation and in practice to Ontario credit unions; OM not available to a credit union. Facts plead general retail raise with no representation of membership limitation, extra-provincial Quebec/New Brunswick issuer, and non-accredited zero net asset offeree. Member/provincial nexus not made out on facts as pleaded. On that reading E is non-compliant.
Current round shows a strengthening issuer-based argument for E with multiple colleagues aligning A and E as paired issuer-based exemptions, but the majority of strict exam readers still treat A as the only unambiguously compliant distribution on the facts as pleaded, with E remaining the principal split point.

Unresolved carried forward: exact territorial/member limitation of the Ontario credit-union/co-operative exemption for an extra-provincial caisse populaire and whether the exemption is truly blanket issuer based or member limited; whether foreign bank debt is covered by the Canadian bank-debt exemption; whether the bank exemption is strictly debt-only or could extend to equity. B, C and D remain non-compliant on prevailing reading.

reflection_text.3:
The Ontario prospectus regime in Jan 2020 is OSA s.53 duty displaced by OSA s.73/74 and NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501. 
Accredited investor = net assets ≥ $1,000,000 excl. principal residence or net income ≥ $200k individual / $300k with spouse in each of two most recent years and reasonably expected in current year. Minimum amount s.2.5 = $150k. OM s.2.9 NI 45-106 is expressly not available to a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company.

Consensus that has stabilised
* A. Bank of China (Canada) is a Schedule II Bank Act bank, bonds = non-convertible debt. The Canadian bank/financial institution debt exemption OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.7 is issuer and security based, not conditioned on accreditation, minimum amount or number of purchasers. Retail bond distribution is prospectus exempt. A is unanimous/textbook.
* C. Private issuer shares to a non-connected individual with salary $35k and net assets $10k. No accredited investor, no $150k minimum amount, no family/friends/business associates, no OM pleaded. Unanimously prospectus required.
* B majority: bank debt exemption is for debt of a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act Canada carrying on business in Canada. JPMorgan Chase is a US chartered parent, not a Bank Act Canada bank. No accredited/minimum amount/OM basis is pleaded for a large Canadian retail offering. Majority now B non-compliant. Minority Colleagues 1,12 persist that bank status + debt is sufficient and foreign domicile does not defeat the exemption.

Disputed points
* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank, distribution is of shares i.e. equity. Majority reading: Ontario bank/financial institution statutory exemption is a debt securities exemption; NI 45-106 s.2.9 OM unavailable to banks; no accredited/minimum amount basis for bank equity to retail including zero net asset unemployed purchaser. Hence prospectus required. Minority Colleagues 5,7 argue the bank exemption is issuer based and applies to any security of a qualifying bank irrespective of form and purchaser net worth, so D would be compliant. Minority remains small.
* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated cooperative credit association/caisse populaire. Split persists and is the main unresolved point.
Broad issuer-based reading, Colleagues 1,5,7,11,12: OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 cooperative credit union exemption is issuer based for securities of a cooperative credit union, not purchaser financial condition based, covers membership/share capital, not defeated by retail raise or zero net asset unemployed offeree, not made conditional on membership at time of offer nor territorially limited to Ontario-incorporated credit unions. On that reading E is compliant, and Colleague 1/11/5/7 now present E as the clean issuer-based equity analogue to A, Colleague 12 even arguing E is cleaner than A because A carries Schedule II teaching doubt.
Strict members/nexus reading, Colleagues 10,2,3,4,6,8,9: the Ontario exemption is in practice a members’ securities exemption for membership/share capital issued to members in accordance with enabling legislation and in practice to Ontario credit unions; OM not available to credit union. Facts plead a general retail raise aimed at a large number of retail investors in Ontario, no representation of membership status, extra-provincial New Brunswick/Quebec caisse, zero net asset unemployed offeree. No accredited/OM/minimum amount exemption available. On that strict reading prospectus required.

Changes in belief and remaining uncertainty
I previously saw A unambiguously compliant, B and C clearly non-compliant, D non-compliant on conventional debt-only reading, and E contested. After round 3 the consensus on A is reinforced. B non-compliance remains majority despite persistent foreign-bank minority. D debt-only reading remains dominant. E remains central split: issuer-based credit union argument has been aggressively advanced in this round by Colleagues 1,11,5,7,12 with Colleague 11 and 1 now treating E as compliant alongside A on consistency grounds, Colleague 12 moving to treat E as the more clearly exempt distribution than A due to Schedule II nuance, while Colleagues 10,2,3,4,6,8,9 maintain the members-only/extra-provincial strict reading and conclude only A is unambiguously exempt.

Unresolved questions
Does the bank debt exemption require the issuer to be Schedule I/II listed Canadian bank or is ‘bank carrying on business in Canada’ sufficient for JPMorgan Chase? Does the Ontario credit union/co-operative exemption extend to a federally incorporated caisse populaire making a general retail share offering to non-members in Ontario, or is it limited to member shares issued to members in accordance with cooperative legislation and in practice to Ontario credit unions? And does the Ontario bank exemption extend to equity of a bank or is it strictly debt?

On a most conservative statutory reading only A is unambiguously prospectus-exempt on the facts pleaded; on a broader issuer-based credit union reading A and E are compliant, with B,C,D non-compliant.

* Issuer/security based for non-convertible debt of a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company carrying on business in Canada under Bank Act/Insurance Companies Act etc. NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.7 / OSA s.74. Not conditioned on accreditation, eligible investor, minimum amount or retail nature. OM s.2.9 expressly unavailable to a bank/trust/loan/insurance company.
* A: Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank; securities are bonds = non-convertible debt. Text-book Canadian bank debt exemption. Unanimous in round 3 as compliant. Minor nuance raised about Schedule II but majority treat as qualifying.
* B: JPMorgan Chase is a U.S. chartered bank, not a Bank Act Canada Schedule I/II/III bank. No s.2.3 accredited investor / s.2.5 $150k minimum amount / s.2.7 family/friends/business associates / s.2.9 OM basis pleaded for large Canadian investor pool. Unanimously non-compliant.
* D: Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank but the exemption is debt only. Distribution is of shares i.e. equity. OM unavailable to banks. No accredited/minimum amount basis made out for a broad retail pool including $0 net asset unemployed purchaser. Round 3 consensus: non-compliant on conventional debt-only reading.

Private issuer
* C: Private issuer shares to unrelated individual. Salary $35k, net assets $10k. Accredited investor Jan 2020 = net assets ≥ $1M ex principal residence or net income ≥ $200k individual / $300k with spouse in each of last two years and reasonably expected current year. Also need $150k minimum amount, family/friends/business associates, or OM. All not pleaded. Unanimously non-compliant.

Credit union/co-operative
* E: Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated cooperative credit association/caisse populaire. OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 s.2.33 / Rule 45-501 co-operative/credit union exemption.
Split persists:
  - Pure issuer-based reading: exemption is securities of the issuer, purchaser neutral, not conditioned on accreditation, eligible investor, minimum amount, membership at time of offer, or provincial incorporation for a trade in Ontario. Zero net asset/unemployed offeree irrelevant, just as retail nature is irrelevant to bank debt in A. On that reading E is compliant and is the credit-union analogue of A, covering equity. Colleagues 1,5,7,11,12 argue this consistency.
  - Strict members-only/provincial nexus reading: exemption is in practice a members’ securities exemption applied to membership/share capital issued to members in accordance with enabling legislation, and in practice to Ontario credit unions; OM not available to credit unions. Member nexus / Ontario nexus not made out. Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,9,10 maintain this reading.

reflection_text.6:
The Ontario regime in force Jan 2020 is OSA s.53/74, NI 45-106 and OSC Rule 45-501. Core issue is issuer-based vs purchaser-based exemptions.

* A – Bank of China (Canada) bonds to retail
Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 s.2.32 / Rule 45-501 s.2.7 is an issuer and security based exemption for non-convertible debt of a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company carrying on business in Canada. The exemption is not conditioned on accreditation, eligible investor status, minimum amount or size of offering. Bonds are debt. Consensus across the group is unanimous that A is prospectus exempt. A minority note a teaching doubt about Schedule II/foreign-owned Canadian bank nuance, but no credible counter-argument remains that A is non-compliant on the facts pleaded.

* B – JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large number of Canadian investors
The Canadian bank/financial institution exemption requires a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act Canada. JPMorgan Chase is a U.S. chartered bank, not a Bank Act Canada bank. No s.2.3 accredited investor, s.2.5 $150k minimum amount, s.2.7 family/friends/business associates or s.2.9 OM basis is pleaded for a general public offering. Majority Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 hold B non-compliant. The minority foreign-bank-as-bank view from round 0 is now isolated.

* C – private issuer shares to non-connected individual salary $35k, net assets $10k
Accredited investor Jan 2020 thresholds: net assets ≥ $1M ex principal residence or net income ≥ $200k individual / $300k with spouse in each of last two years and reasonably expected in current year. Eligible investor OM thresholds $75k income / $400k net assets. No $150k minimum amount, no OM risk acknowledgement, no family/friends/business associates relationship pleaded. Consensus is C is prospectus-required.

* D – Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to retail pool including zero net asset unemployed purchaser
Fairstone is a Bank Act bank. The Ontario bank/financial institution exemption is widely read as a debt-securities exemption. NI 45-106 s.2.9 OM is expressly unavailable to a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company. Majority Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 maintain the conventional debt-only reading, so bank equity is not covered and a retail share distribution with a non-accredited purchaser is prospectus-required. Minority Colleagues 5,7 argue the bank exemption is issuer-based and covers shares irrespective of form and purchaser condition. Majority view prevails in the group.

* E – Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to large retail pool including zero net asset unemployed purchaser
Principal unresolved split.

Issuer-based reading: Colleagues 1,5,7,11,12 argue OSA s.74 and NI 45-106/Rule 45-501 cooperative credit union exemption is issuer-based for securities of a cooperative credit union/caisse populaire, not conditioned on purchaser accreditation, net worth, membership status at offer or provincial nexus. On that reading the retail character, zero net asset/unemployed offeree and extra-provincial incorporation are irrelevant, just as for A. The exemption also covers equity, making it broader than the bank debt exemption. Colleague 12 adds that A carries a Schedule II teaching doubt, making E the cleaner pure issuer-based example.

Members-only/nexus reading: Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 treat the exemption as a members’ securities exemption for membership/share capital issued to members in accordance with enabling legislation, in practice applied to Ontario credit unions. The facts plead a general retail raise aimed at a large number of retail investors with no representation take-up is limited to members, issuer is extra-provincial New Brunswick/Quebec, and OM is unavailable to a credit union. On that strict reading the membership/provincial nexus is not made out and no accredited/OM/minimum amount exemption is available. E is then non-compliant as pleaded.

Working beliefs updated: A is clearly compliant under Canadian bank-debt exemption. B, C and D are non-compliant on the conventional debt-only / Canadian-bank reading and the facts given. E remains the principal unresolved point with a persistent issuer-based vs members-only split; on the conventional exam teaching set the only unambiguously compliant distribution is A, with E being the main disagreement and B the secondary foreign-bank disagreement that has now largely converged to non-compliance. The group is converging on A as the settled example, while the consistency argument for a pure issuer-based credit-union exemption keeps E alive as the counter-argument.

The discussion is now anchored on A as the uncontested baseline and on the B/C/D consensus, with E as the remaining split.

A – Bank of China Canada bonds to retail. Uncontested across the group. Schedule II Bank Act bank, non-convertible debt. OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.7 is issuer and security based and not conditioned on accreditation, minimum amount, eligible investor status or size. Retail bond raise is prospectus exempt in Ontario as of Jan 2020.

B – JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large number of Canadian investors. Consensus in round 3: non-compliant. The Ontario bank/financial institution exemption is a Canadian Bank Act exemption engaged for debt of a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act Canada. JPMorgan Chase is a U.S. chartered bank, not a Bank Act Canada bank. No s.2.3 accredited investor, s.2.5 $150k minimum amount, s.2.7 family/friends/business associates or s.2.9 OM basis is pleaded for a large public-style offering. Prospectus required. Earlier minority view that domicile is irrelevant to “bank” status has been dropped by Colleague 1 in this round.

C – private issuer shares to a non-connected individual with salary $35k, net assets $10k. Consensus non-compliant. Accredited investor thresholds Jan 2020: net assets ≥ $1M ex principal residence or net income ≥ $200k single / $300k with spouse in each of last two years and reasonably expected current year. No $150k minimum amount, OM or relationship pleaded. Prospectus required.

D – Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including zero net asset unemployed purchaser. Majority view persists: the Ontario bank/financial institution statutory exemption is a non-convertible debt securities exemption; NI 45-106 s.2.9 OM is expressly unavailable to a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company. Equity of a bank is not covered and no accredited/minimum amount basis is made out. Prospectus required. Minority Colleagues 5,7 maintain an issuer-based reading that would cover bank equity irrespective of form/purchaser; that view is rejected by the majority in round 3.

E – Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to large retail pool including zero net asset unemployed purchaser. Split persists and is sharpened.

Broad issuer-based reading, advanced by Colleagues 1,5,7,11,12: Ontario cooperative credit union/co-operative exemption under OSA s.74 and NI 45-106/Rule 45-501 is issuer based, not purchaser financial condition based, and covers securities of a cooperative credit union / caisses populaires. Unemployed/zero net assets does not defeat it; the exemption is purchaser neutral like the bank-debt exemption. Members-only and Ontario-incorporation glosses are overstated practice descriptions, not statutory conditions, and extra-provincial federal cooperative credit associations are recognised. On that reading E is prospectus exempt and is argued as the cleanest retail share example, even cleaner than A because the bank exemption carries a Schedule II teaching doubt.

Strict/members-only reading, advanced by Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,9,10: exemption is a members’ securities exemption applied to membership/share capital issued to members in accordance with enabling cooperative/credit union legislation and in practice to Ontario credit unions; OM is also unavailable to a credit union. Facts plead a general retail raise aimed at a large number of retail investors with no representation of membership limitation, an extra-provincial New Brunswick/Quebec caisse, and a non-accredited zero net asset offeree. On that strict reading member/provincial nexus not made out and prospectus required.

Unresolved questions remaining: whether Ontario credit-union/co-operative exemption applies to an extra-provincial caisse populaire and to a general retail raise with no member limitation; whether the bank-debt exemption requires a Bank Act Canada charter or is satisfied by any bank; whether bank exemption ever covers equity.

Current belief: A is unambiguously prospectus exempt. B, C and D are non-exempt on the stated facts under the conventional reading. E remains the main contested item. On the conventional strict members-only/extra-provincial reading E is non-compliant, making A the only clearly compliant distribution. If the broad pure issuer-based credit-union reading is accepted, E joins A as compliant, and several colleagues now argue E is in fact the more clearly exempt distribution than A.

Bank of China Canada is a Schedule I/II/III Bank Act Canada bank. OSA s.74 / NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.7 is an issuer and security based statutory exemption for non-convertible debt securities of a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company carrying on business in Canada. Bonds are non-convertible debt. The exemption is not conditioned on accreditation, eligible investor status, a minimum amount, the size of the offering or the retail character of the offerees. A retail bond distribution by a Bank Act Canada bank is therefore prospectus exempt in Ontario. A is the textbook Canadian bank debt example and is uncontested on the facts pleaded.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large Canadian pool
The bank/financial institution exemption is a Canadian Bank Act exemption. NI 45-106 s.2.32 / OSA s.74 is engaged for debt of a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act Canada. JPMorgan Chase is a U.S. chartered bank, not a Bank Act Canada bank. No s.2.3 accredited investor, s.2.5 $150,000 minimum amount investment, s.2.7 family/friends/business associates or a qualifying s.2.9 offering memorandum basis is pleaded for a general public style Canadian offering. Prospectus required.

C. Private issuer shares to a non-connected individual salary $35k net assets $10k
A private issuer distribution to a person with no connection can only rely on s.2.3 accredited investor, s.2.5 minimum amount, s.2.7 family/friends/business associates/employee or s.2.9 OM. Accredited investor Jan 2020 is net assets ≥ $1,000,000 ex principal residence or net income ≥ $200,000 individual / $300,000 with spouse in each of the last two years and reasonably expected in the current year. Salary $35,000 and net assets $10,000 are well below the test. No $150k minimum amount, no OM and no relationship is pleaded. Prospectus required.

D. Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to a broad retail pool including a zero net asset unemployed purchaser
Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank but the Ontario statutory bank/financial institution exemption is a non-convertible debt securities exemption. NI 45-106 s.2.9 OM is expressly unavailable to a bank, trust company, loan company or insurance company. The securities are shares, i.e. equity. No accredited investor / $150k minimum amount basis is made out for bank equity to a broad retail pool. On the conventional debt only reading bank equity is not covered and a prospectus is required.

E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to a large retail pool including a zero net asset unemployed purchaser
Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a cooperative credit association / caisse populaire federally incorporated under the Cooperative Credit Associations Act and falls within the NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501 definition of a cooperative credit union. OSA s.74 and NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 provide an issuer based prospectus exemption for securities of a cooperative credit union. The exemption is framed as securities of the issuer, not as a purchaser financial condition or membership test. On the same policy logic that makes the retail nature of the offerees irrelevant to the bank debt exemption in A, the personal financial circumstances of an offeree, the retail breadth of the raise and the absence of an accredited investor / $150k minimum amount / OM condition are irrelevant to the availability of the issuer based credit union / co-operative exemption. The zero net asset / unemployed fact pattern is purchaser neutrality in the same way the retail nature of the Bank of China bond raise is purchaser neutrality for the bank debt exemption.

On a consistent issuer based reading of the Ontario exemptions in force in January 2020 A is the classic Canadian bank debt example and E is the clean issuer based credit union / co-operative example for a broad retail share raise. B, C and D remain non compliant on the stated facts. On the conventional strict members only / extra provincial gloss sometimes applied in exam commentary E is contested, in which case the only distribution that is unambiguously prospectus exempt on the facts as stated is A, the Bank of China Canada bond distribution.
